subject: pathology
title: Gallbladder, biliary and pancreatic pathology

steps.tx: Gallstones are classified by chemical composition into three main types. **Cholesterol stones** form in supersaturated bile, and **pigment stones** are black in haemolysis or brown in infected bile. Acute cholecystitis causes a positive Murphy sign, whereas Charcot triad indicates cholangitis and Courvoisier law redirects painless jaundice toward malignancy.
steps.say: Cholesterol stones form because bile becomes supersaturated with cholesterol over time gradually. Black pigment stones occur in haemolysis whereas brown stones form in infected bile. Murphy sign indicates cholecystitis because inspiratory arrest occurs on palpation typically. Courvoisier gallbladder indicates malignancy because painless jaundice accompanies a palpable gallbladder.

vis.alt: A composite image showing three distinct types of gallstones: yellowish cholesterol, dark black pigment, and friable brown pigment stones.
vis.caption: Gallstones classified by chemical composition: cholesterol, black, and brown

steps.tx: Gallbladder cancer presents late and biliary emergencies are separated by classic triads. **Gallbladder cancer** is linked to large stones and a **porcelain gallbladder**, and cholangitis requires urgent drainage with antibiotics. Gallstone ileus causes obstruction with pneumobilia, whereas Mirizzi syndrome results from an impacted cystic duct stone compressing the hepatic duct.
steps.say: Gallbladder cancer presents late because early disease causes few specific symptoms initially. Porcelain calcification is associated with malignancy and large stones increase risk substantially. Cholangitis requires drainage urgently because infected bile causes sepsis very rapidly. Bowel obstruction occurs because an ectopic gallstone impacts in the ileum distally.

steps.tx: Acute pancreatitis is autodigestion of the pancreas triggered most often by gallstones or alcohol. **Acute pancreatitis** causes epigastric pain radiating to the back, and **serum lipase** is more specific and persists longer than amylase. Contrast imaging stages severity, and infected necrosis requires drainage whereas sterile necrosis is usually observed carefully.
steps.say: Pancreatitis causes epigastric pain because autodigestion inflames the gland and retroperitoneum intensely. Pain radiates to the back and leaning forward relieves it in many patients. Lipase is preferred because specificity is higher and elevation persists longer diagnostically. Infected necrosis requires drainage whereas sterile necrosis is observed carefully usually.

steps.tx: This contrast CT shows a dark non enhancing area within the pancreas with surrounding stranding. **Pancreatic necrosis** fails to enhance after contrast, and **peripancreatic fluid** with fat stranding is shown around the gland. This appearance matters because necrosis determines severity and the later risk of infected necrosis in acute pancreatitis.
steps.say: This scan shows pancreatic tissue that fails to enhance after contrast administration clearly. Surrounding fat is stranded and fluid collects around the inflamed gland extensively. Necrosis indicates severe disease because dead tissue risks secondary infection later. Severity scoring is performed because imaging extent predicts complications accurately.

vis.alt: Axial contrast CT showing nonenhancing pancreatic necrosis with peripancreatic stranding and fluid.
vis.caption: Contrast CT showing pancreatic necrosis with peripancreatic stranding. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Chronic pancreatitis destroys gland function and pancreatic tumours differ greatly in risk. **Chronic pancreatitis** causes steatorrhoea and diabetes, and **pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma** causes painless jaundice with a double duct sign. Serous cysts are benign with a central scar, whereas mucinous and main duct lesions require resection or close surveillance.
steps.say: Chronic pancreatitis calcifies the gland because repeated inflammation destroys tissue progressively over years. Steatorrhoea develops because lipase secretion is lost earliest among enzymes typically. Ductal cancer causes painless jaundice and weight loss in elderly patients characteristically. Double duct dilation indicates malignancy because pancreatic and bile ducts obstruct together.
